title: {{cast.mary}}'s agent calls {{vocab.resourceTool}}, rehearsed offline
goal: {{cast.mary}}'s agent needs to call tools on {{vocab.resourceTool}} on {{cast.mary}}'s behalf. You can show the whole flow with no sign-in and no tenant.
obstacle: The agent starts with a grant, an ID-JAG, and a resource server must not accept that as a key. It has to be traded for an access token first, and the server must refuse anything else.
control: ID-JAG in mock mode: a sample PingFederate issues the ID-JAG, a sample authorization server redeems it for an access token, and the sample resource server accepts only that token. Everything is sample data in the browser and nothing is sent.
say: Even with no network and no tenant, we can show every step, and what the server accepts and what it refuses.

steps.title: Nothing to sign in to
steps.tell: Mock mode needs no sign-in. The page is marked Mock: sample data, nothing is sent, and every step uses sample data in the browser.
steps.say: This runs with no sign-in and no tenant, so it cannot fail on the day.
steps.why: A rehearsal that cannot break, before the live demo.

steps.title: Request the ID-JAG
steps.tell: Request ID-JAG returns a sample from the sample PingFederate: typ oauth-id-jag+jwt, addressed to the sample authorization server, valid for 300 seconds, for the sample subject user.0042.
steps.say: The grant is short-lived and addressed to one authorization server.
steps.why: A grant that could be replayed anywhere would be a bearer token by another name.

steps.title: Redeem it
steps.tell: The sample authorization server trades the ID-JAG for an access token (typ at+jwt, valid for an hour). Under Scope to request, leave all scopes or pick just mcp:read: the token carries no more than the ID-JAG's scope. The authorization server's record of the redemption is shown, marked as a sample.
steps.say: The access token can carry less than the grant, never more.
steps.why: The resource owner's side decides what is actually granted.

steps.title: The agent calls {{vocab.resourceTool}}
steps.tell: List tools shows the sample tools search_records, get_record and create_note, and notes that delete_record is hidden from this token by scope (it needs mcp:admin). Results are sample data.
steps.say: The agent sees only what its token allows.
steps.why: The tools the agent never sees are the ones it cannot be tricked into calling.

blocked.tell: Switch Resource to REST API, then try without a token and with the raw ID-JAG. Both are refused with 401: no Authorization: Bearer header, or an ID-JAG that is a grant for the authorization server to redeem, never an access token for a resource.
blocked.say: The grant is not a key, and the server says exactly why.

steps.title: Run the refusals
steps.tell: Run all shows four sample refusals, each with an OAuth error and no token: a replayed ID-JAG, a tampered signature, a different client, and a scope the IdP did not grant.
steps.say: A real authorization server refuses all four, and this shows what that looks like.
steps.why: A grant you cannot refuse is not a control.

steps.title: Revoke and prove it
steps.tell: Revoke and retry shows a sample control exchange that works, a sample revocation of the refresh token, and then a refused retry.
steps.say: Once the session is revoked, no new grant is issued.
steps.why: In mock mode the revoke, like everything else here, is sample data.

blocked.tell: The sample retry is refused with invalid_request, and the verdict reads Proved: PingFederate refused a new ID-JAG (invalid_request).
blocked.say: After the revoke, the same request gets nothing.

proof.happy: The decoded sample access token: issued by the sample authorization server, audience the sample MCP resource, scope no wider than the ID-JAG's.
proof.blocked: The resource page's 401 for no token or for the raw ID-JAG, naming the failed check, and the sample OAuth errors from the refusals.
